name: binary search on a grid
hook: You can binary search a 2D matrix without ever flattening it.
hook_slide: Binary search a 2D matrix. *No flattening needed.*
hook_sub: It's a sorted array wearing a grid costume.
caption: Search a 2D Matrix makes two promises: each row is sorted, and each row starts above where the previous one ended. Chain them and the whole grid, read row by row, is one sorted sequence.
So binary search the index range 0 to rows × cols − 1 and turn each midpoint k back into a cell: row = k // cols, col = k % cols. The flattened array is never built.
On a {big} × {big} matrix that's at most {worst} cell reads instead of {cells}.
When a problem hands you a stronger promise, use it.
What does k = 6 map to in a 3 × 4 grid? 👇

p: Each row is sorted, left to right.
